blocking_failures: anti_cheating_measures: The traffic_sampler.c source file is available to the agent in the environment (environment/app/src/traffic_sampler.c) and the Dockerfile only removes /tmp/traffic_sampler.c after compiling. The C source reveals the exact seq%7==3 filter and the weight*0.5 adjustment rule. Tests in test_outputs.py rely precisely on these implementation details (comments explain the math assuming seq%7==3 drops). An agent can read the source to trivially understand the sampler's behavior without reverse-engineering the binary.

valid_failure_modes: Tests T3 and T7 rely on precise sampler behavior (seq%7==3 filter and weight*0.5 for errors after 20 samples) that is described in sampler-protocol.md only at a high level. The test comments spell out the exact math assuming specific filter behavior. The weight halving after 20 samples is a nuance of the binary that is NOT documented in sampler-protocol.md (the protocol says weight field is for weighted averaging, but does not mention the sampler adjusting weights). An agent implementing a correct weighted error rate using original weights (not sampler-adjusted weights) might fail T3/T7 if the boundary conditions differ from what the test assumes, because the test expects sampledErrorRate > 0.10 based on specific count assumptions.
